# Choose data and reference resources

Use SpaMTPData to retrieve an experiment and SpaMTPdb to retrieve its annotation
references. This guide loads paired mouse-brain data, inspects the reference
registry and annotates two measured bladder ions. Pinning both resource
versions records which data and references were used.

| Package | Responsibility | Primary representations |
|---|---|---|
| SpaMTPData | Discoverable experiment resources | Cardinal, SpatialExperiment, auxiliary files; labelled historical archives |
| SpaMTPdb | Versioned annotation and pathway resources | Independent tables/lists with checksums and provenance |
| SpaMTP | Analysis, annotation, plotting and explicit conversion | Existing Bioconductor S4 containers and public accessors |

Package, RaMP and experiment-data releases have separate versions. The calls
below specify the resource versions used in this guide.

## Installation and example scope

All three packages are installed from Bioconductor:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install(c("SpaMTP", "SpaMTPdb", "SpaMTPData"))
```

`citation("SpaMTP")` supplies the package reference.

This guide combines mouse-brain mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) and paired
RNA with a mouse-bladder MSI panel and pinned RaMP annotation resources.
Resources are downloaded on first use unless a verified local or cached copy
is available.

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(SpaMTPdb)
library(SpaMTPData)
```

# Data to a native analysis container

## Native experiment structure

```{r native-data}
spe <- spaMTPData("mouse_brain_dhb_striatum", version = "1.1.0")
spe
```

The complete archived striatal dataset retains all measured mass features and
locations. It was previously selected by MSI clusters from one brain section.
Paired RNA in `altExp(spe, "SPT")` shares location names with MSI; independent
measurements require alignment and mapping before pairing.

## Normalization and spatial display

First establish an expression scale and inspect a measured ion in tissue
coordinates. `LogNormalize` adds `logcounts` using the base-2
transformation `log2(1 + 10000 * intensity / total_intensity)`. The same layer
supplies the two principal components requested by `npcs = 2`.
Figure 3.\@ref(fig:preprocess) displays the measured mass nearest m/z 400.14659,
a focal feature in the original mouse-brain tutorial. Compare its distribution
with the archived anatomy and side labels in the
[complete workflow](End_to_End_Workflow.html).

```{r preprocess, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, out.width="450px", fig.cap="Measured m/z 400.14659 across all archived mouse-brain striatal locations. Each point retains its original image coordinates, with y increasing downwards; colour shows LogNormalize intensity."}
spe <- normalizeSMData(spe, "LogNormalize", verbose = FALSE)
spe <- runMetabolicPCA(spe, npcs = 2, assayName = "logcounts", verbose = FALSE)
feature <- findNearestMZ(spe, 400.14659)
plotSpatialFeature(spe, feature,
    assayName = "logcounts",
    labels = sprintf("m/z %.4f", rowData(spe)[feature, "mz"]), pointSize = 1.3
)
reducedDimNames(spe)
```

Retrieve the embedding with `reducedDim(spe, "pca")`.
`metadata(spe)$reduction_inputs$pca` records the expression layer and features
used for PCA.

# Find database resources

`spaMTPDatabaseInfo()` lists available database resources and their versions.

```{r database-registry}
registry <- spaMTPDatabaseInfo(version = "3.0.7")
registry[
    registry$resource %in% c("chem_props", "smiles_features", "pathway"),
    c("resource", "version", "r_data_class", "bytes", "md5")
]
```

## Load reference tables

`loadSpaMTPDatabase()` loads the selected reference tables.
Use `offline = TRUE` to reuse verified local files or cached downloads.
Set `localDir` to the directory containing the published RDS files when
staging resources on a shared system.

```{r production-resources}
database <- loadSpaMTPDatabase(c("chem_props", "pathway"), version = "3.0.7")
dim(database$chem_props)
```

`attr(database$chem_props, "spamtp_database")` exposes the resource version,
source URL and expected checksum for recording alongside analysis results.

# Measured bladder ions and RaMP candidates

The bundled bladder subset retains the spatial extent and all 79 features of
an archived annotated panel. Select its two ions nearest m/z 741.53058 and
798.54114 for a concise annotation example, retaining every supplied location.
Their historical labels are stored separately in `archived_lipid_candidates`.

`buildMZAnnotationIndex()` indexes the verified RaMP `chem_props` table using
potassium adducts (`M+K`, positive mode). `annotateSM()` searches within 5 ppm;
`minScore = 0` retains matched candidates for review. The database's
precomputed structure features are reused automatically. `annotationCandidates()`
lists the stored candidate records for each measured ion, ranked by score.

```{r annotation}
bladder <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "bladder_demo.rds", package = "SpaMTP"))
ions <- bladder[findNearestMZ(bladder, c(741.5305786, 798.5411377)), ]
index <- buildMZAnnotationIndex(database$chem_props,
    adducts = "M+K", polarity = "positive"
)
annotated <- annotateSM(ions,
    index = index, adducts = "M+K",
    polarity = "positive", ppm = 5, minScore = 0,
    returnOnlyAnnotated = FALSE, saveIntermediate = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
rowData(annotated)[, c("mz", "archived_lipid_candidates")]
candidates <- annotationCandidates(annotated, distinct = FALSE)
table(candidates$feature)
head(candidates[, c("feature", "rank", "IsomerNames", "Adduct", "Error", "Score")])
annotationInfo(annotated)
```

## Candidate records

The archived alternatives are SM 34:1 / PA 37:1 and PC 34:1 / PE 37:1;
SM, PA, PC and PE denote sphingomyelin, phosphatidic acid, phosphatidylcholine
and phosphatidylethanolamine. Each ion matches multiple RaMP records under the
stated adduct
and mass tolerance; individual records can group several isomers. The
[annotation tutorial](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html) shows candidate
scores, ranking and index reuse.

# Published native datasets and historical archives

The default resource release, `1.1.0`, provides seven native SpatialExperiment
datasets with URLs and hashes in
[Zenodo record 22733262](https://zenodo.org/records/22733262).
Historical Seurat files remain explicitly available in release `1.0.0`.

`metadata = TRUE` returns resource names, versions and data classes.
`native_metadata` describes release 1.1.0; `archive` describes the same
resource's historical 1.0.0 Seurat file.

```{r inspect-native}
native_metadata <- spaMTPData("mouse_brain_fmp10", metadata = TRUE)
native_metadata[, c("resource", "version", "r_data_class", "requires_conversion")]
```

```{r inspect-archive}
archive <- spaMTPData("mouse_brain_fmp10", version = "1.0.0", metadata = TRUE)
archive[, c("resource", "version", "r_data_class", "requires_conversion")]
```

## Direct native-data retrieval

The call below retrieves the same mouse-brain dataset acquired with
2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB) matrix and paired Visium RNA in `SPT`.
It reuses the verified local or cached resource from the first retrieval.
`version = "1.1.0"` pins the data release independently of the package version.

```{r read-published-native}
native <- spaMTPData("mouse_brain_dhb_striatum", version = "1.1.0")
altExpNames(native)
```

## Convert a historical Seurat object

This example uses SeuratObject to convert the archived data to
SpatialExperiment. `legacy` is the historical
FMP-10 object: `assay = "Spatial"` selects MSI and `image = "fov"` selects
coordinates. `converted_archive` has 1,538 features and 3,005 locations.

```{r convert-archive, eval=requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)}
legacy <- spaMTPData("mouse_brain_fmp10", version = "1.0.0")
converted_archive <- seuratToSpatialExperiment(legacy, assay = "Spatial", image = "fov")
converted_archive
```

See [modern data access](Modern_Data_Access.html) for coordinate and layer
selection and [the native workflow](SpaMTP_Bioconductor.html) for
analysis. The [migration table](Modern_Data_Access.html#migrating-existing-scripts)
lists common historical calls and their native replacements.

Continue with [metabolite annotation](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html) to
inspect score components, candidate ambiguity and the effect of a score cutoff.
